parsed.explanation: The division inherits the national regime, which carries documented traveller-facing exposure: sex-marker restrictions on passports, a case-note entry screen with a possible lifetime fraud ineligibility finding, reported passport confiscations, and immigration-custody abuse of transgender detainees. Parent-level hostility is also documented, including a terrorism framing of 'radically pro-transgender' groups and a national lever to subpoena hospital records. Against this, the division has documented, in-force protections: a public-accommodations ban covering hotels, restaurants and shops, a gender-identity hate-crime enhancement, repeal of the gay and trans panic defence, a conversion-therapy ban, no division-level facility ban, and enforceable shield laws. Enforcement records for the accommodations and hate-crime protections are not sourced, so I credit them only partly. The national layer is contested in court and several orders are enjoined, which tempers the national deduction. The net lands in the reduced-risk band, below an unexposed independent state.
